papers.title: Multidomain progression phenotypes in Parkinson's disease: Five-year trajectories in the COPPADIS cohort.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) progression is heterogeneous and is incompletely represented by single-domain outcomes. We identified multidomain progression phenotypes over five years in the prospective multicenter COPPADIS cohort and examined baseline predictors and external clinical validity. Among 694 participants with PD, 497 with sufficient longitudinal data were analyzed across motor severity, motor complications, non-motor burden, cognition, functional independence, and health-related quality of life. Individual annual slopes were standardized and directionally harmonized; Gaussian mixture modeling identified progression classes. Healthy controls (n = 207) provided a longitudinal reference. Two classes were supported by Bayesian information criterion and clinical parsimony: slow/relatively resilient (n = 319, 64.2%) and accelerated multidomain progression (n = 178, 35.8%). Accelerated progressors worsened significantly faster in all six domains. Baseline freezing-of-gait severity was the strongest independent marker of accelerated progression (OR 1.58 per SD, 95% CI 1.22-2.06), followed by higher levodopa-equivalent daily dose (OR 1.35, 95% CI 1.03-1.77). Compared with healthy controls, accelerated progressors showed excess cognitive decline and worsening depressive symptoms and fatigue, whereas the slow/resilient group showed no significant control-referenced differences after multiplicity correction. Accelerated progression was also associated with first hospitalization (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.16-2.42), emergency-department attendance (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.08-1.83), and incident falls (HR 2.19, 95% CI 1.56-3.08). Five-year PD progression segregates into clinically meaningful multidomain phenotypes with distinct prognostic profiles.

papers.title: Skin biopsy-derived measures of small-fiber loss relate to cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cognitive impairment is common in Parkinson's disease (PD), but accessible peripheral tissue correlates remain limited. We examined whether skin biopsy-derived intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD) and the phosphorylated α-synuclein (P-SYN) structural involvement score differed across cognitive groups and were independently associated with cognitive performance. METHODS: This single-center cross-sectional study included 126 patients with normal cognition (PD-CN; n = 30), mild cognitive impairment (PD-MCI; n = 35), or dementia (PDD; n = 61). Biopsies were obtained from posterior cervical and distal-leg sites. Mean IENFD was averaged across sites, whereas the Total P-SYN score summed site-specific scores. Trend, correlation, regression, and exploratory ROC analyses were performed. RESULTS: Mean IENFD decreased and the Total P-SYN score increased across cognitive groups (both P for trend < 0.001). After age adjustment, the group difference in Mean IENFD remained significant (P = 0.005). In the fully adjusted model, Mean IENFD remained positively associated with MoCA score (standardized β = 0.238, P = 0.003), whereas the Total P-SYN score did not (β = -0.051, P = 0.423). The measures were modestly inversely correlated (ρ = -0.333, P < 0.001). Combined-model AUCs were 0.802 for PD-MCI/PDD versus PD-CN and 0.851 for PDD versus PD-CN, but did not significantly outperform Mean IENFD alone. CONCLUSION: Skin biopsy-derived small-fiber loss was independently associated with poorer global cognitive performance in PD. The Total P-SYN score differed across cognitive groups but was not independently associated after adjustment. Mean IENFD may represent a peripheral correlate of cognitive performance and warrants longitudinal validation.

papers.title: Identification and validation of biomarkers associated with mitochondrial dynamics dysfunction in Parkinson's disease based on GEO datasets.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD), the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, is characterized by an unclear etiology and a lack of specific early diagnostic biomarkers. This study investigated novel biomarkers associated with mitochondrial dynamics (MD) dysfunction in PD. METHODS: Transcriptomic data from the Gene Expression Omnibus database (training set: GSE6613, n = 72; validation set: GSE99039, n = 438) and 23 MD-related genes (MDRGs) were integrated. Differentially expressed genes were screened using the limma package. Three machine learning algorithms (random forest, support vector machine, and generalized linear model) were employed to construct diagnostic models. Feature importance analysis identified key candidate biomarkers, which were preliminarily validated in clinical samples via reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, and compound prediction analyses were subsequently performed. RESULTS: Cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 2 (CYSLTR2) and alpha‑tocopherol transfer protein‑like gene (TTPAL) were identified as MDRG score-correlated biomarkers. In the validation set, CYSLTR2 was significantly downregulated (log2FC = -1.25, P < 0.001) and participated in neuroactive ligand-receptor interactions. Conversely, TTPAL was significantly upregulated (log2FC = 1.52, P < 0.001) and associated with the pathogenic Escherichia coli infection pathway. Immune analysis revealed six differentially infiltrated immune cell types. Notably, TTPAL expression was positively correlated with keratinocytes (cor = 0.30, P = 0.031). Four potential therapeutic compounds were predicted. RT-qPCR suggested the downregulation of CYSLTR2 and upregulation of TTPAL in patients with PD (P < 0.0001). CONCLUSION: This study identified CYSLTR2 and TTPAL as novel candidate biomarkers associated with MD

papers.title: Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder as a model of early neurodegeneration: challenges for research and clinical diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (RBD) has evolved from a descriptive parasomnia to a clinically informative model for studying early neurodegenerative processes, particularly within the spectrum of α-synucleinopathies. Defined by the loss of REM sleep atonia and the emergence of dream enactment behaviors, RBD reflects dysfunction of brainstem circuits that normally suppress motor output during dreaming. Longitudinal evidence indicates that many individuals with isolated RBD eventually develop neurodegenerative disease, most commonly Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, or, less frequently, multiple system atrophy, positioning RBD among the most specific clinical markers of prodromal synucleinopathy currently recognized. Mechanistic studies suggest that RBD arises from instability within distributed REM sleep regulatory networks involving dopaminergic, noradrenergic, serotonergic, and cholinergic systems. This network dysfunction may precede classic motor and cognitive symptoms and can be accompanied by early abnormalities in neurophysiology, imaging, cognition, olfaction, autonomic function, and molecular biomarkers. These findings support a model in which RBD may represent one of the earliest clinically accessible manifestations of a multisystem neurodegenerative process, although anatomical origin, propagation patterns, and phenoconversion trajectories vary across patients. Despite these advances, clinical management remains largely symptomatic, and key challenges persist in diagnosis, risk stratification, prognostic counselling, and therapeutic development. A broader clinical framework is therefore needed, in which RBD is not viewed solely as an isolated sleep disorder but also as a potential marker of early neurodegeneration in appropriately characterized patients. papers.title: Neuroinflammatory Biomarkers in Neurodegenerative Disease Diagnosis and Progression.
papers.abstract: Neuroinflammatory markers are now key tools for diagnosing and monitoring neurodegenerative diseases. These biomarkers are associated with the activation of the immune system in the central nervous system, which is associated with the disease process. This review highlights some selected aspects of the neuroinflammatory markers, cytokines, chemokines, and markers of glial activation, and their role in diseases such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and multiple sclerosis. Recent innovations in molecular and imaging technology have led to better identification and measurement of neuroinflammatory biomarkers in CSF, blood, and brain tissue. These approaches allow noninvasive monitoring and assist in the integration of biomarker profiles coupled with clinical evaluation for better diagnostic accuracy and patient stratification. Fluctuations in neuroinflammatory markers are associated with disease activity and cognitive impairment, which suggest these markers as potential early diagnostic and prognostic indicators. Using a biomarker profile in addition to clinical information helps better distinguish among neurodegenerative disorders and monitor therapeutic outcomes. Although promising, challenges remain in standardising biomarker measurement and interpreting biomarker specificity, given overlapping inflammatory pathways between diseases. There is ongoing research to confirm biomarker panels that can reliably differentiate between neurodegenerative disorders and track treatment effects. Decoding the multifaceted crosstalk between neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration is essential for developing targeted therapies that modulate immune processes and slow disease progression. Neuroinflammatory biomarkers are useful diagnostic and prognostic tools that can aid in the clinical management and the development of new treatment strategies in neurodegenerative disorders.

papers.title: Evaluation of cross-cohort generalizability of machine learning-derived blood transcriptomic biomarkers for Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) lacks reliable, minimally invasive diagnostic biomarkers, and blood transcriptomic machine learning (ML) has emerged as a potential discovery strategy, although cross-cohort reproducibility remains uncertain. We performed a leakage-free analysis of four publicly available transcriptomic datasets (GSE99039, GSE6613, GSE7621, and GSE54536) using a nested ML framework in which data-dependent preprocessing and model development were restricted to training data. Eleven classifiers were evaluated using a training-fold-derived 100-gene panel with repeated 5-fold cross-validation, independent validation, and exploratory cross-tissue comparison, complemented by WGCNA and functional enrichment analysis. The ensemble achieved a mean discovery AUC of 0.682 ± 0.049 in GSE99039, whereas independent validation in GSE6613 yielded an AUC of 0.618 (95% CI, 0.470-0.767). Cross-tissue evaluation in substantia nigra GSE7621 produced an AUC of 0.549 with 51% direction-of-change concordance. WGCNA showed only weak module-trait associations, while the ML panel was predominantly enriched for immune processes, including natural killer cell immunity, myeloid leukocyte activation, and antigen presentation. These findings indicate limited generalizability of blood transcriptomic ML signatures and support further validation in larger, harmonized multicenter cohorts.

papers.title: IFI-ML: a novel framework combining Fuzzy Inference and Machine Learning for Parkinson's disease classification.
papers.abstract: Early detection of Parkinson's Disease (PD) remains challenging due to vocal signal complexity and severe data imbalance, which necessitates that machine learning (ML) models deliver higher classification accuracy. This study aims to break the systematic, inverse trade-off between sensitivity and specificity in voice-based PD classification. We present the Intelligent Fuzzy Inference and Machine Learning (IFI-ML) framework, an uncertainty-aware architecture utilizing entropy-based partitioning, hybrid classifiers, and a Sugeno Type-2 Fuzzy Inference System (FIS). While traditional frameworks apply global resampling techniques such as the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) or Random Over-Sampling (ROS) across entire datasets, the proposed IFI-ML framework utilizes information gain-driven clustering to segment samples into sensitive (uncertain boundary) and non-sensitive partitions. The framework optimizes conventional ML classifiers on the stable, non-sensitive clusters, while routing critical boundary samples to the Type-2 FIS to handle local class overlap without distorting the overall data distribution. papers.title: Skin Seed Amplification Assay Differentiates Multiple System Atrophy from Parkinson's Disease.
papers.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Misdiagnoses of multiple system atrophy (MSA) and Parkinson's disease (PD) remain common. OBJECTIVE: The objective of the study was to develop a skin α-synuclein seed amplification assay (αSyn-SAA) for detecting pathological α-synuclein and distinguishing MSA from PD. METHODS: In this blinded, cross-sectional study, 308 skin biopsies from 117 participants were analyzed using a standardized thioflavin T fluorescence-based αSyn-SAA protocol. The cohort included 42 PD, 31 MSA, 30 controls, and 14 progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) cases. Kinetic parameters were analyzed to differentiate PD from MSA, and matched skin cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) analyses were performed. Assay thresholds were predefined using brain lysates from neuropathologically confirmed cases. Fibril morphology from amplified skin samples was compared to postmortem brain using proteinase K digestion and electron microscopy. RESULTS: αSyn-SAA detected synucleinopathy (PD or MSA) with 82.2% sensitivity and 90% specificity versus controls. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis showed that maximum fluorescence (Fmax CONCLUSION: Skin αSyn-SAA detects pathological α-synuclein in living patients with high accuracy and distinguishes MSA from PD based on assay kinetics and fibril strain properties, supporting its potential as a biomarker to distinguish among synucleinopathies. © 2026 The Author(s). papers.title: Gender differences in depressive-like behavior in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: A Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by both motor and non-motor symptoms, including depression, which markedly impairs patients' quality of life. Although sex differences have been described in PD progression, the mechanisms underlying gender-specific susceptibility to depressive symptoms remain poorly understood. METHODS: This study investigated sex-dependent differences in depressive-like behaviors and their underlying molecular mechanisms in an in vivo model of 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP)-induced dopaminergic degeneration, using adult male and female CD1 mice. RESULTS: Our results demonstrated that MPTP administration induced nigrostriatal degeneration and α-synuclein accumulation in both sexes, with more pronounced alterations in males. Male mice also exhibited greater depressive- and anxiety-like behaviors, accompanied by a marked reduction in 5-HT2C receptor expression, increased hippocampal acetylcholine levels, impaired expression of the synaptic markers PSD-95 and synaptophysin, and a stronger downregulation of the BDNF/PI3K/AKT pathway compared with females. DISCUSSION: These findings demonstrate that sex significantly influences vulnerability to PD-associated depressive symptoms, with males showing greater behavioral and molecular impairment. Overall, our results highlight the importance of considering sex as a biological variable in PD research and support the development of personalized therapeutic strategies targeting non-motor symptoms.

papers.title: MemTrax as a scalable digital triage tool for mild cognitive impairment screening: primary validation in Alzheimer's disease and exploratory analysis in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) pose escalating global health challenges, with early detection of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) being critical for timely intervention. The 2023 Delphi consensus highlights the need for scalable tools suitable for primary care. This study aimed to validate the MemTrax as a rapid memory-focused triage tool against consensus-recommended cognitive assessments, including the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), for detecting MCI due to Alzheimer's disease (AD-MCI) as the primary objective, and to explore its performance in MCI due to Parkinson's disease (PD-MCI) as an exploratory aim, evaluating its utility as a rapid, accessible digital tool. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study enrolling 222 participants: 74 with AD-MCI, 73 healthy controls (HCs; primary cohort); 42 PD patients with normal cognition (PD-NC), 33 with PD-MCI (exploratory cohort). All participants underwent MMSE, MoCA and MemTrax testing. Diagnostic accuracy, optimal cut‑offs, and correlations between MemTrax parameters (percent correct [MTx‑%C], reaction time [MTx‑RT], composite score [MTx‑Cp]) and standard cognitive measures were evaluated. RESULTS: In the primary AD cohort, MTx-%C showed an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.876 (95% CI: 0.813-0.926) for discriminating AD-MCI from HCs, comparable to MoCA (AUC = 0.879) and MMSE (AUC = 0.916). At a cut-off of ≤ 80%, MTx-%C achieved a sensitivity of 70.3% and specificity of 90.4%. In the exploratory PD cohort, MTx-%C (AUC = 0.808) showed similar discrimination to MMSE (AUC = 0.694) in differentiating PD-MCI from PD-NC (DeLong's test, p = 0.142). Multivariate analysis of MTx-%C, MTx-RT, and MTx-Cp demonstrated significant separation between MCI and cognitively normal groups in both the AD and PD cohorts. MTx-%C showed significa

papers.title: Differential and directional body coupling analysis in Parkinsonian gait.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder primarily characterized by motor impairments and altered whole-body coordination. Objective and accessible approaches for quantifying inter-limb and cross-directional coupling during gait remain limited in clinical settings. Using a prospectively collected dataset of individuals with PD and healthy controls (HC), we propose a comprehensive analytical framework based on human pose estimation to extract time-series kinematic signals from key body landmarks. Coupling strengths between body segments were quantified to characterize whole-body coordination patterns. Statistical filtering identified discriminative body coupling factors that significantly differentiated PD from HC. The identified factors demonstrated clear and consistent alterations in coordination patterns across groups. Furthermore, multiple machine learning classifiers validated their discriminative capacity, achieving robust classification performance. Correlation analyses between the top 10 pre-specified directional body coupling factors and MDS-UPDRS III scores demonstrated modest but statistically significant associations in the full PD cohort (n = 121), with 8 of 10 factors surviving FDR correction (ρ=0.27-0.31). These associations suggest that directional body coupling metrics capture clinically relevant variation in motor impairment severity beyond binary PD versus HC discrimination and may serve as potential digital biomarkers of PD-related motor dysfunction. Subtype-stratified analyses were conducted only as exploratory supplementary analyses, and larger, more balanced subtype cohorts are required before subtype-specific conclusions can be drawn. Overall, body coupling metrics provide reliable biomechanical markers of PD-related gait impairment and support the clinical potential of this non-invasive and cost-effective pipeline for early diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring.

papers.title: Efficacy of cognitive behavioral therapy for anxiety and depression symptoms in Parkinson's disease patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anxiety and depression are highly prevalent non-motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease (PD), severely compromising health-related quality of life. Conventional pharmacological management is frequently constrained by adverse effects, polypharmacy, and pharmacokinetic interactions. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) represents a promising structured non-pharmacological strategy, but an updated, comprehensive synthesis of clinical trial evidence is warranted. OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the efficacy and clinical safety profile of CBT for alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients with PD. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to October 2025. RCTs evaluating CBT (≥ 4 sessions over ≥ 4 weeks) versus control conditions (e.g., treatment as usual, waitlist, active controls) in adults with PD reporting anxiety and/or depression outcomes were included. Two reviewers independently screened literature, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled via random-effects models. Subgroup, sensitivity, and publication bias analyses were performed. RESULTS: Twenty-one RCTs comprising 892 patients with PD (CBT: n = 465; control: n = 427) were included. papers.title: Utilization of neurosurgical modalities for Parkinson's disease in Southeast Asia.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Neurosurgical advancements in Parkinson's disease (PD) treatment can significantly improve symptoms. However, the use of these modalities in Southeast Asia (SEA) faces barriers. METHODS: We conducted an online cross-sectional survey among movement disorder specialists in SEA. Respondents provided country-level estimates of utilization, targets, financial coverage, and limitations in the utilization of four neurosurgical modalities. RESULTS: Six out of the seven countries reported neurosurgical treatment for PD. Deep brain stimulation (DBS) was reported to be available in 6 countries, averaging 16.2 ± 4.8 procedures yearly. Radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RFT) and magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound (MRgFUS) were reported in three and two countries, respectively, while no respondent reported the use of gamma knife radiosurgery for PD. Funding issues and patient-related factors were the most commonly reported barriers. Out-of-pocket payments remained the primary funding source for surgeries in 66% of countries, with the cost of DBS ranging from USD 32,000.00 to 50,500.00. CONCLUSIONS: This survey provides preliminary respondent-reported estimates of DBS, RFT, and MRgFUS utilization across participating SEA countries. DBS volumes were lower than the published estimates from neighbors in the Western Pacific Region. The lack of funding and patient factors are commonly reported factors that may limit the use of these neurosurgical treatments.

papers.title: Time to Move Upstream? A Framework for Expanding the Focus of Freezing of Gait to Prodromal, Subclinical, and Pre-FOG Stages.
papers.abstract: Freezing of gait (FOG) is one of the most disabling motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease, yet a fundamental question remains unresolved: why does FOG occur at any given moment? Most research has focused on studying FOG once it is already manifest. The present work aims to synthesize recent observations and propose a conceptual framework in which FOG reflects a dynamic process unfolding across multiple stages and time scales. Subtle changes in gait dynamics and physiology can precede episodes by several seconds (Stage -1), and experimental paradigms show that individuals without clinically recognized freezing may exhibit brief episodes under sufficiently sensitive conditions (Stage -2). At longer time scales, prospective studies indicate that vulnerability to freezing may be detectable years before onset (Stage -3). This framework reflects the idea that FOG emerges from progressive instability across interacting motor, cognitive, autonomic, and environmental systems, rather than as an isolated event. The proposed framework includes a prodromal stage, a subclinical stage, an immediate prefreezing state, and the freezing episode itself (Stage 0). This framework integrates findings from wearable sensing, physiology, and clinical studies and emphasizes that FOG remains latent in Stage -3, may be elicited only under specific conditions in Stage -2, and becomes manifest as instability evolves toward imminent and overt freezing (Stages -1 and 0, respectively). Reframing FOG as a multistage process that includes an upstream phase raises new questions regarding mechanisms, classification, and intervention, and may, ultimately, inform strategies aimed at predicting and preventing freezing rather than simply reacting to it.

papers.title: Six highlights from Parkinson's disease research.
How a once-controversial idea is advancing understanding of Parkinson's disease.
Advances in plant polysaccharide research for neurodegenerative diseases therapy.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs), including Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), Huntington's disease (HD), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), and multiple sclerosis (MS), represent a growing global public health burden with limited therapeutic options. Plant polysaccharides are natural, biocompatible, and multi-target bioactive macromolecules that have emerged as promising candidates for ND intervention. This review systematically summarizes recent progress in elucidating the structural characteristics, structure-activity relationships, and neuroprotective mechanisms of plant polysaccharides. Key structural features such as molecular weight, monosaccharide composition, glycosidic bond configuration, and spatial conformation critically modulate the biological activity of these molecules. Furthermore, we summarize the numerous protective effects of plant polysaccharides against NDs, including inhibiting abnormal protein aggregation, alleviating oxidative stress via the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway, suppressing neuroinflammation through the NF-κB and MAPK signaling pathways, regulating neuronal apoptosis, and modulating the gut-brain axis. Clinical translation challenges, primarily blood-brain barrier penetration, structural heterogeneity, and insufficient clinical validation, are discussed. Future directions include developing advanced delivery systems, conducting large-scale randomized controlled trials, and exploring synergistic combination therapies. Collectively, plant polysaccharides show considerable promise as potential multi-target candidates for the intervention of NDs, although further studies are needed to clarify their therapeutic potential and facilitate clinical translation.

papers.title: Neuroprotective Effects of Natural Products: Innovative Therapeutic Strategies for Preventing the Progression of Neurodegenerative Diseases.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and other neurodegenerative disorders are serious conditions characterized by progressive neuronal degeneration, which leads to cognitive decline, motor dysfunction, and other neurological problems, severely impairing daily activities and quality of life. These diseases involve multiple biological pathways, including oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and abnormal protein folding. Given the multifactorial nature of neurodegenerative diseases, neuroprotective approaches targeting multiple mechanisms hold great promise for prevention and treatment. Natural products derived from plants, microorganisms, and marine organisms are renowned for their excellent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities and show great potential in preventing neurodegenerative diseases. Unlike synthetic compounds, these naturally sourced bioactive compounds offer a variety of therapeutic targets due to their diverse structures and biological activities. This review provides a systematic overview of 125 newly identified neuroprotective natural products derived from plants, microorganisms, and marine organisms in 2025, with a comprehensive summary of their origins, chemical architectures, and biological activities. These collected natural products are categorized into seven classes based on their structural features: terpenoids (42.4%, 53/125), alkaloids (19.2%, 24/125), glycosides (10.4%, 13/125), lignans (9.6%, 12/125), phenols (6.4%, 8/125), flavonoids (6.4%, 8/125), and other miscellaneous compounds (5.6%, 7/125). Accumulating evidence indicates that natural products hold great promising potential for preventing and slowing the progression of neurodegenerative disorders.

papers.title: Regional Mitochondrial Density Maps Selective Posterior Atrophy in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial dysfunction has been implicated in the pathobiology of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet the spatial relationship between regional energetic demand and patterns of neurodegeneration remains poorly understood, limiting mechanistic insight and development of disease-modifying therapies. OBJECTIVES: This study tested whether regional mitochondrial density aligns with patterns of brain atrophy in PD, how this alignment differs across genetic groups, and whether the mitochondrial-atrophy axis associates with motor and cognitive features. METHODS: Structural magnetic resonance imaging data were analyzed from 849 individuals (210 healthy controls, 639 patients with PD). Principal component analysis (PCA) identified dominant atrophy axes and tested their association with regional mitochondrial density and complex I activity. Transcriptomic validation used Allen Human Brain Atlas gene expression data restricted to 924 MitoCarta-annotated genes across 31 cortical regions. RESULTS: Participants with PD exhibited higher volumetric loss in limbic and subcortical regions than controls. PCA showed a posterior cortical axis of atrophy (PC3) that correlated positively with regional mitochondrial density and was more strongly expressed in LRRK2-PD than in sporadic PD. This axis was selectively associated with visuospatial dysfunction. Transcriptomic validation confirmed that regions of greater atrophy preferentially expressed mitochondrial genes, with mitoribosome assembly, mitochondrial DNA maintenance, and coenzyme Q biosynthesis emerging as the strongest pathway-level predictors. CONCLUSION: These findings link the brain's regional mitochondrial landscape to spatially patterned neurodegeneration in PD, with amplification in LRRK2 mutation carriers. This mitochondrial atrophy axis may provide a biologically informed marker aiding patient stratification and mitochondrial-targeted therapeutic development. © 2026 The Author(s). papers.title: LRRK2 G2019S variant is associated with transcriptional changes in Parkinson's disease human myeloid cells under proinflammatory environment.
papers.abstract: The G2019S mutation in the leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) gene is a major risk factor for the development of Parkinson's disease (PD). LRRK2, although expressed in different cell types, is highly abundant in cells of the innate immune system. Given the importance of central and peripheral immune cells in the development of PD, we sought to investigate the consequences of the G2019S mutation on microglial and monocyte transcriptome and function. We have generated large-scale transcriptomic profiles of isogenic human induced microglial cells (iMGLs) and patient derived monocytes carrying the G2019S mutation in untreated culture conditions and following exposure to the proinflammatory factors IFNγ and LPS. We demonstrate that the G2019S mutation exerts a profound impact on the transcriptomic profile of these myeloid cells, and describe corresponding functional differences in iMGLs. The G2019S mutation led to an upregulation in lipid metabolism and phagolysosomal pathway genes in untreated and LPS/IFNγ stimulated iMGLs, which was accompanied by an increased phagocytic capacity of myelin debris. We also identified dysregulation of cell cycle genes, with a downregulation of the E2F4 regulon. Transcriptomic characterization of human-derived monocytes carrying the G2019S mutation confirmed alteration in lipid metabolism associated genes. Altogether, these findings reveal the influence of G2019S on the dysregulation of the myeloid cell transcriptome under proinflammatory conditions.

papers.title: HIV-1 Tat drives genotype-dependent neuroimmune programs that promote Parkinson Disease-like neurodegeneration in the hSNCAA53TGba1 mouse model.
papers.abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus type I (HIV-1) infection can induce both motor and cognitive impairments even in patients receiving combination antiretroviral therapy (cART). These neurological alterations are related to direct and indirect mechanisms represented by viral and immune mediated processes, respectively. HIV-1 directly elicits neurological damages through some viral proteins including transactivator of transcription (Tat), a protein involved in the HIV-1 replication and able to affect neural cell through autocrine and paracrine pathways. In this study, we investigated the functional and transcriptional effects of intrastriatal Tat injection in pre-symptomatic mice carrying the hSNCAA53T
